questions.stem: Which two all-round lights in a vertical line, at or near the masthead, identify a vessel on pilotage duty?
options: Red over white
Green over white
Red over green
White over red
questions.explanation: Rule 29(a)(i) gives white over red ("white over red, pilot ahead"). Red over white is fishing other than trawling, green over white is trawling, and red over green is the optional sailing vessel signal.

questions.stem: At night you see white over red all-round lights at a masthead and a red sidelight below. What is she and what is she doing?
options: A vessel not under command, making way
Pilot vessel on duty, underway, port side
A fishing vessel making way, showing her port side
A pilot vessel at anchor
questions.explanation: White over red is the pilotage signal, and a sidelight means she is underway, here showing her port side. Fishing would be red over white. At anchor she would show anchor lights instead of sidelights. NUC is two reds.

questions.stem: A pilot vessel on duty is waiting at anchor for an inbound ship. What does she show at night?
options: Anchor lights only, like any other vessel
Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
White over red, sidelights and sternlight
White over red, plus anchor lights
questions.explanation: Rule 29(a)(iii): at anchor she adds the Rule 30 anchor light, lights or shape to her white over red. Sidelights and sternlight are for underway. Anchor lights alone would hide that she is on duty, and two reds mean not under command.

questions.stem: A 16 m power-driven pilot boat has finished her duties and is returning to base. What lights should she show?
options: White over red only, until she reaches base
Power-driven lights for her length
White over red, sidelights and sternlight
A blue flashing light
questions.explanation: Rule 29(b): a pilot vessel not engaged on pilotage duty shows the lights or shapes prescribed for a similar vessel of her length, here an ordinary power-driven vessel. The pilot lights are only for pilotage duty, and the blue flashing light is a Canadian government identification signal.

questions.stem: Which statement about the signals in Rule 29 is correct?
options: By day a pilot vessel on duty shows a ball over a cone
A pilot vessel on duty shows a masthead light above her white over red
No day shape; underway: white over red, sides, stern
A pilot vessel on duty shows white over red only when at anchor
questions.explanation: Rule 29 lists white over red, plus sidelights and sternlight underway, or anchor signals at anchor. It lists no masthead light and no day shape. The white over red is shown underway as well as at anchor.
